card.name: Mohiniyattam
card.era: Term first attested 16th century; systematized 18th-19th c; revived 1930
card.tagline: Kerala's graceful solo lasya 'dance of the enchantress'
card.profile: Mohiniyattam is an Indian classical dance from Kerala, named after Mohini, the female enchantress avatar of Vishnu (Wikipedia). Following the gentle, feminine lasya style of the Natya Shastra, it is traditionally a solo dance by women, with delicate swaying movements, subtle facial expression, Carnatic-style music and lyrics in the Sanskrit-Malayalam hybrid Manipravalam (Wikipedia). The term is first attested in the 16th-century Vyavaharamala; the dance was systematized under Travancore king Swathi Thirunal but later ridiculed and banned (1931-38) during the colonial anti-nautch movement before being revived (Wikipedia).
card.insight: Mohiniyattam was revived and reconstructed largely through poet Vallathol Narayana Menon, who founded the Kerala Kalamandalam in 1930 to restore Kerala's classical arts (Britannica).
